signals.title: Do not consult the query context when building a CAST
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109946 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR: Context has expired` exception when a stored expression containing `accurateCastOrDefault` or a `to<Type>OrDefault` function is evaluated after the query that created it has finished, for example a `MATERIALIZED` column default on `INSERT` or a mutation expression. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109946 `CastOverloadResolverImpl` inherited `WithContext`, which holds only a `weak_ptr<const Context>`, and its `buildImpl` passed `getContext()` to `createFunctionBaseCast`. That is safe only during analysis, while a caller still holds a strong `ContextPtr`. #109946 made `FunctionCastOrDefault` store that resolver as a member and call `build()` at execute time. The `ActionsDAG` keeps the resolver alive but nothing keeps its context alive, and both affected paths build the DAG from a function-local `Context::createCopy` that dies on return (`inplaceBlockConversions.cpp:230` for materialized-column defaults, `MutationsInterpreter.cpp:1762` for mutations). Evaluating such an expression later throws `Context has expired`: an exception in release builds, a server abort under debug and sanitizers. This captures the conversion settings in the resolver's constructor, while the context is provably alive, and has `buildImpl` consume that snapshot. `FunctionCast` used its `ContextPtr` for nothing but `settings(context, ...)`, so the snapshot moves one step earlier in the same call chain rather than being introduced. The resolver now holds no context at all, so the `WithContext` exception for this file in `various_checks.sh` is removed. The two build paths keep their distinct `DateTimeOverflowBehavior`: `Saturate` for `createInternalCast`, `Ignore` for `buildImpl`. Sharing one snapshot between them would silently change date-time conversion. Since a snapshot replaces a live context, every context-derived conversion setting was compared before and after and is byte-identical, including all three `date_time_overflow_behavior` modes, `cast_keep_nullable`, `precise_float_parsing`, the IPv4/IPv6 error settings and timezone substitution. `04510_accurateCastOrDefault_settings` from #109946 passes unchanged. The new test aborts a master server at `CastOverloadResolver.cpp:195` and passes with this change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. The defect rides along with #109946, so it is present wherever that landed: 26.7 (#114689, merged); the 25.8, 26.3 and 26.5 backports are still open. <details> <summary>CI provenance</summary> `Logical error: Context has expired`, STID `1805-460a`, first seen 2026-08-13 22:45:16 UTC, about four hours after #109946 merged. The frame pair `CastOverloadResolverImpl::buildImpl` + `Context has expired` has no earlier occurrence in the 90 days CIDB retains. | when (UTC) | check | where | |---|---|---| | 2026-08-14 02:20:39 | [Stress test (arm_release)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=17d2798b962607ded301a9cab913c8ca70a33409&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29) | master, `17d2798b9626` | | 2026-08-14 01:49:18 | [AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114666&sha=dc79add25489c923c36b67be101b349bb964b190&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29) | unrelated PR | | 2026-08-14 00:02:12 | [Stress test (amd_tsan)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114131&sha=06852ededde08f411d205aea05f6a78dbadaf55c&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29) | unrelated PR | | 2026-08-13 22:50:06 | [AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100374&sha=50f4e25e8e3204407e724392592231c2ac54151c&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29) | unrelated PR | | 2026-08-13 22:45:16 | [AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112679&sha=a2d3810c4df7a6d108a1a5b207e779cc41ae7e86&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29) | unrelated PR | The master row is bucketed as STID `1805-4810` because an STID is a stack hash, but it carries both discriminating frames and `17d2798b9626` contains #109946. </details>

signals.title: Read and checksum the UNIQUE KEY dense-index SST through IDataPartStorage
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow the UNIQUE KEY to work on encrypted and remote disks by reading and writing its dense-index SST through the part storage abstraction; the SST is now recorded in `checksums.txt`. ### Description The per-part UNIQUE KEY dense index (`unique_key_index.sst`) was opened and written by local filesystem path, which only worked on local disks and left the sidecar outside the part's checksum accounting. This PR drives the SST through `IDataPartStorage` using a custom RocksDB `Env`(a read-only `FileSystem` over `IDataPartStorage::readFile` for the reader, a `WriteBuffer`-backed one for the writer), so encrypted and remote disks work as well. The SST is now recorded in `checksums.txt`, so it is transferred by backup/fetch like any other part file and validated by `checkConsistencyBase`: a missing or wrongly-sized SST fails the standard consistency check and the part is detached as broken, while size-preserving corruption is caught at load time by `ensureValidDenseIndex` (RocksDB block-checksum + entry-count validation), which removes and rebuilds the index. On readonly storage a corrupt or absent SST fails the load closed instead of activating an unprobeable part. The previous restriction that UNIQUE KEY tables must reside on local-only storage policies is removed.

signals.title: Fix lost wakeup of restarting thread on startup from the attach thread
signals.text: A schedule request on a deactivated task is a silent no-op. On startup from the attach thread the restarting thread runs inline with its task activated only afterwards, so when a failed previous startup attempt had deactivated the task, the retry scheduled from inside the inline attempt was lost and nothing ever scheduled the task again: the table stayed readonly until an unrelated session expiry. Schedule the task after activating it; this also restores the periodic session-expiration check, lost the same way when the inline attempt succeeds. signals.title: Throw instead of reporting success for an unsupported OPTIMIZE
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114765 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114765 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `OPTIMIZE TABLE` on an object-storage table whose engine does not implement compaction reported success while doing nothing. It now raises an error, like every other engine that does not support the statement. This affects `DeltaLake`, `Paimon`, `Hudi` and plain object-storage engines (`S3`, `GCS`, `COSN`, `OSS`, `AzureBlobStorage`, `HDFS`, and object-storage-backed `URL`); `Iceberg`, which does implement compaction, is unchanged. Closes #114765. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114765#issuecomment-5291252538); reported by @ zlareb1. `StorageObjectStorage::optimize` overrides the throwing `IStorage` default and forwards to `configuration->optimize`, which resolved to one of two defaults returning `false`. `InterpreterOptimizeQuery` discards that `bool`, so the statement reported Ok. Verified: three parquet files and a four-file `_delta_log`, unchanged before and after. The fix goes into those two defaults, not the wrapper. `IStorage.h` documents the return as "whether any work has been done", and `StorageMergeTree` relies on that for a legitimate no-op under `optimize_throw_if_noop`, so reading `false` as "unsupported" at the wrapper would mislabel an implementation that ran and did no work. Both forwarders are untouched. Two defaults, reached by disjoint engine sets: `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration::optimize` (plain configurations) and `IDataLakeMetadata::optimize` (the 4 non-Iceberg lake metadata classes). `optimize` was the only unsupported-operation default in either header returning a value instead of throwing. Iceberg is unaffected: it is the sole override and never returns `false`. Its `allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction` gate is asserted as a control. Two error codes, as elsewhere in these headers: plain object storage `NOT_IMPLEMENTED (48)`, lakes `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD (1)` naming the lake type. One line to unify if you prefer one code. No setting or format change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry, and no doc change (the support matrix has a `Compaction` row only in the Iceberg tab). 0 stateless and 0 integration tests affected: every existing `OPTIMIZE` on an object-storage engine is Iceberg, and the `S3`/`Azure` hits are `MergeTree` on an object-storage disk. BuzzHouse absorbs the new error (`disallowed_error_codes` is unset in `buzzhouse_job.py`, `compare_success_results` pinned `False`). Hudi has no local engine, so it is covered by sharing `IDataLakeMetadata::optimize` with the Delta and Paimon arms.

signals.title: Stop exchange sinks when the consumer needs no more data
signals.text: A distributed-plan query with a satisfied `LIMIT` kept all upstream stages running to completion: an exchange sink consumed and dropped the rest of the stream after the consumer sent `NoMoreDataNeeded`, so the client received the result while the query kept running until cancelled. Now the sink closes its input instead, and the stop propagates backward through the stages the same way a local `LimitTransform` stops its producers. The in-memory exchange reader also detaches when its output port is closed, not only on cancellation. The new test covers a `LIMIT` in the middle of the plan: the stage that satisfies it finishes early and the stop crosses two exchange layers down to the scans. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A distributed plan query (`make_distributed_plan`) now stops its upstream stages when a `LIMIT` is satisfied, instead of computing the full result and discarding it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Keep the column default when another MODIFY COLUMN restates the type
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a single `ALTER` with two `MODIFY COLUMN` subcommands on the same column silently corrupting that column's default: a default set by one subcommand was dropped, and a `REMOVE DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED`/`ALIAS` was undone, whenever a following subcommand restated the column type. ### Description Two `MODIFY COLUMN` subcommands on one column silently corrupted its default in two opposite directions, from plain DDL, returning success and logging nothing. Wrong results: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (event String, c UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple(); ALTER TABLE t MODIFY COLUMN c UInt32 MATERIALIZED JSONExtractUInt(event, 'x'), MODIFY COLUMN c UInt32 CODEC(T64, LZ4); INSERT INTO t (event) VALUES ('{"x":42}'); SELECT c FROM t; -- 0, expected 42; default_kind was empty ``` Valid input rejected: `MODIFY COLUMN c REMOVE MATERIALIZED, MODIFY COLUMN c UInt32 CODEC(...)` left the `MATERIALIZED` in place, so a later `INSERT INTO t (event, c)` failed with `ILLEGAL_COLUMN` where it succeeds after a plain `REMOVE`. Omitting the type was already correct, so one token decided whether it worked. `AlterCommand::apply` replaced the column default whenever the subcommand carried a data type, writing an empty default over what a preceding subcommand had written into the shared metadata copy. `AlterCommands::prepare` compensated by back-filling from the table, but it reads the pre-ALTER column: nothing to back-fill for a default just set, and a stale default to resurrect for one just removed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113853#discussion_r3737650442 The default is now replaced only when the subcommand carries a default expression, and the back-fill is gone, making `MODIFY_COLUMN` match `ADD_COLUMN`. One accepted statement starts being rejected: dropping a `MATERIALIZED` that made the column nullable while restating the type as non-nullable now reports the conversion it cannot perform, as those statements issued separately already do. New test `04904` fails on the parent commit and passes with the fix; 50/50 randomized runs are green. A 55-test ALTER neighbour set ran on both binaries: nothing fails only with the fix. Also noticed, not addressed here: an existing default unreadable as the new type is rejected even with a single `MODIFY COLUMN`, pre-existing in `validate()`.

signals.title: Fix TopK filtering dropping NULL and NaN rows from the answer
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113406 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107074 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` silently omitting rows that belong in the answer when the sort column contains a `NaN` or a nested `NULL` and TopK filtering is active. A `Float32`/`Float64`/`BFloat16` column holding `NaN` was affected at default settings; nested-`NULL` types such as `Array(Nullable(T))` and `Map(K, Nullable(V))` were affected under `ASC NULLS FIRST` and `DESC NULLS LAST` with `use_top_k_dynamic_filtering_for_variable_length_types` enabled. Also fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` for a sort column of type `Tuple(Dynamic)` or `Tuple(Variant(...))`. ### Description TopK filtering must order values the way the sorter does. In three cases it did not, rejecting a row that belongs in the top `n`. `__topKFilter`'s fast path compares through `lessOrEquals`/`greaterOrEquals`. For a composite type those resolve to `GenericComparisonImpl`, which hardcodes the nan/nulls-direction hint to "NULLs and NaNs are greatest" and so contradicts `ORDER BY` whenever `nulls_direction` is -1. For a float, IEEE comparison leaves `NaN` unordered against every value including itself, while the sorter treats `NaN` as tying with itself, so a `NaN` row fails both comparators at every direction. Separately, `use_skip_indexes_for_top_k` ranks granules through `MinMaxGranuleItem::operator<`, a bare `Field` comparison running before any read, losing the same rows with the dynamic filter off. The fix routes these sort columns to the existing general path, which already honours `nulls_direction`, and adds floats to the two skip-index eligibility gates. Those gates already excluded `Nullable` and collations for the same reason; floats were missed because they are number-represented yet admit `NaN`. The float predicate comes from `WhichDataType::isFloat` plus a recursive `forEachChild` walk rather than a list of wrapper types, so `BFloat16`, `Tuple(Float64, ...)`, `Array(Float64)` and typed `JSON` are covered. `Object`, `Variant` and `Dynamic` answer true unconditionally: their contents are known only at runtime. The new test runs every carrier with filtering on and off and requires the two to agree: of its 35 pairs, on the unmodified binary 20 disagree, 4 abort, and the 11 control pairs already agree. Cost: granule pruning is now unavailable for float sort columns. On a NaN-free `Float64` column, 10M rows, `ORDER BY f ASC LIMIT 10` goes from a median 7 ms to 15 ms and reads 10M rows instead of 81,920; an integer column is unaffected (6 ms, 81,920 rows on both). Making `MinMaxGranuleItem` order-aware would recover this, as the `TODO` in the code notes.

signals.title: Propagate OpenTelemetry trace context into AsyncTaskExecutor fibers
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112738 The OpenTelemetry trace context is stored in a `FiberLocal`, but the fibers created by `AsyncTaskExecutor` (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`) started with an empty fiber-local context. Remote queries of a distributed query were parented directly to the trace context supplied by the client, bypassing the spans of the initiator, and no spans were produced for the async tasks themselves. ## Changes - `AsyncTaskExecutor` captures `OpenTelemetry::CurrentContext()` on the thread that constructs it and installs a `TracingContextHolder` inside the fiber routine. This seeds the fiber-local context from the creating query and opens one span per task execution, named after the executor (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`). It is a no-op when tracing is not enabled. - `Fiber` destruction fixes - `Fiber::local_data` is now keyed by `typeid(T).name()` instead of the address of the `FiberLocal` object, so the same fiber-local variable resolves to the same data from every shared object. ## Span hierarchy change Remote queries now descend from the initiator through the `Connection::sendQuery` CLIENT span instead of appearing as direct children of the client-supplied trace context: ``` client span └─ query (initiator) └─ Connection::sendQuery [CLIENT] └─ query (remote server) ``` The expectations of `01455_opentelemetry_distributed` are updated accordingly: only the initial query span is now a direct child of the input trace context. This is the first part of the distributed tracing improvements discussed in the linked issue; instrumentation of the distributed query plan is left for follow-up pull requests. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Propagate the OpenTelemetry trace context into the fibers used for asynchronous connection establishment and remote query execution (hedged requests, `async_socket_for_remote`, `async_query_sending_for_remote`). Spans of remote queries in a distributed query are now correctly parented under the initiator's `Connection::sendQuery` span instead of being attached directly to the client-supplied trace context, and each asynchronous task execution produces its own span.

signals.title: Resolve the 25.8 cherry-pick conflict of #112327
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112327 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114796 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a use-after-free when a `LEFT JOIN` to a dictionary with `join_algorithm = 'direct'` had a join key that is serialized `Sparse`. `getColumnVectorData` returned a `PaddedPODArray` reference into a column owned only by a function-local `ColumnPtr`, so the dictionary lookup read freed memory. ### Description Backport of #112327 to `25.8`. The robot cherry-pick #114796 is `CONFLICTING`, so the automation cannot carry it. The conflict is in one file. `getColumnVectorData` materializes its key column with `removeSpecialRepresentations` on master and with `recursiveRemoveSparse` here; `removeSpecialRepresentations` does not exist on this branch. The resolution keeps 25.8's call and takes the fix's predicate, so the resolved change is the same 8 insertions and 7 deletions as the merged commit. On this branch the copy therefore guards `Const` and `Sparse`; `ColumnReplicated` does not exist here and is dropped from the comment's carrier list. `25.8` is affected. On the official `25.8.30.17` binary the repro (a 2M-row sparse probe joined to a `FLAT()` dictionary) segfaults in 2 of 7 runs, and with jemalloc junk filling it fails 4 of 4 with `Invalid number of rows in Chunk ... expected 65409, got 0`. The same data written densely passes. Comparing returned values alone cannot see this, because freed but intact memory still yields the correct numbers. Verified in both directions with a clang-19 Debug build, this branch's pinned compiler, asserting build ids against the running server. Pristine `25.8` aborts on the first assertion of the ported test, at `PODArray::operator[]` inside `FlatDictionary::hasKeys` reached through `IDictionary::getByKeys` and `DirectKeyValueJoin::joinBlock` - the mechanism reported on master. With the fix the test passes and the repro returns the correct result in 3 of 3 runs. One branch adaptation in the test: `enable_lazy_columns_replication` does not exist on `25.8` and is rejected as an unknown setting, so it is dropped from the `ARRAY JOIN` statement. The statement and every assertion are kept.

signals.title: Fix TSan data race on `std::cerr` in `gtest_filecache.cpp`
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Unit tests (tsan)` fails with a data race on the format state of the global `std::cerr` object. TSan runs with `halt_on_error=1`, so the report aborts the binary: 2172 of 19839 tests had run, and the rest lost coverage for that run. ``` SUMMARY: ThreadSanitizer: data race contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/ios:497 in std::__1::ios_base::width() const Location is global 'std::__1::cerr' of size 264 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114666&sha=000cc7f7a20b3f741b10fa78b6b643a6e0a16683&name_0=PR&name_1=Unit%20tests%20%28tsan%29 The character sink is locked; the `ios_base` members are not: libc++ reads `width()` and writes `width(0)` on every `operator<<`, and both stacks end there. Root cause: `src/Interpreters/tests/gtest_filecache.cpp` wrote the same stream under two different synchronisation disciplines. `FileCacheTest::SetUp` points the Poco root logger at a `ConsoleChannel(std::cerr)`, which serialises its writers under a static mutex (TSan's `M0`), so any thread that logs writes `cerr` while holding it. The file additionally performed 36 raw `std::cerr <<` writes, which take no lock. The second writer here is `ExternalLoader::PeriodicUpdater::doPeriodicUpdates` logging its startup line: the updater runs because the shared unit-test context leaves `application_type` at `SERVER`. This removes the unsynchronised writer. The 14 bare `"Step N"` markers are deleted (a failing `ASSERT_*` already reports file and line); the remaining diagnostics go through the logger, so every write takes the same lock, including the file's two worker threads. The logger is obtained on first use: a logger keeps whatever channel the root had when created, so one created before `SetUp` would silently drop every message. The redirection itself is untouched, so `FileCacheTest.LoadMetadataParallelism`, which asserts on captured stderr, still passes. Validated with a TSan build (clang-22, as pinned for the CI job). A harness forcing repeated `ExternalLoader` startup writes concurrently with the test reproduces the signature above before the change and produces none after it. Diagnostic output and all 37 `FileCacheTest.*` results match in both arms. 17 other gtest files write `std::cerr` raw (excluding commented-out code), which the style check permits under `/tests/`; this was the only one also installing a channel on it.

signals.title: Convert OUTER join to INNER join by null-rejecting join conditions
signals.text: Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112456 Outer join to inner join conversion works by looking if a filter above the join rejects default values, NULLs in the case of nullable columns. This change allows join conditions of enclosing joins to be used for rejecting NULLs too: 1. optimizer pass `deriveNotNullFiltersFromJoin` derives `col IS NOT NULL` filters and adds them to the plan. 2. these filters get pushed down and used for the conversion as usual. 3. filters derived during planning are compiled away before execution. 4. optimizer pass `promotePlannerOnlyFilters` can promote planner derived filters to executable filters based on their estimated selectivity. #### Performance result from `join_convert_outer_to_inner_by_join_predicates.xml` and `promote_planner_only_not_null_filters.xml` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Convert `OUTER JOIN` to `INNER JOIN` when a later JOIN filters out its NULL-extended rows, and filter NULL join keys directly at the table scan when column statistics show it is selective. Controlled by the new settings `query_plan_convert_outer_join_to_inner_join_by_join_predicates`, `query_plan_promote_planner_only_not_null_filters` and `query_plan_max_selectivity_for_promoting_not_null_filters` (all enabled by default).

signals.title: Run 04869_postgresql_tls_trailing_arguments sequentially
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114580 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114580 `04869_postgresql_tls_trailing_arguments` registers a PostgreSQL database pointing at the unreachable `127.0.0.1:1` and ran in the parallel group. Since `show_remote_databases_in_system_tables` defaults to `true`, that database is visible in `system.tables`, `system.columns` and `system.completions`, so a concurrent query scanning those tables without a database filter connects to the unreachable host. The connection failure is logged on the scanning query's own thread, so it reaches that client's stderr, and `clickhouse-test` fails any test whose stderr is non-empty. The polluter stays green and an unrelated test goes red, which makes the failure unattributable from the victim's side. One master hit since the test landed on 2026-08-13: `00938_fix_rwlock_segfault_long` in `Stateless tests (arm_binary, parallel)`, whose whole body is an unfiltered `system.tables` and `system.columns` scan. [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5c5dd13e2760e7087bd9a7f5e6e6fa572a2b003f&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20parallel%29) I add `no-parallel` with a written justification, matching the sibling `04210_show_remote_databases_in_system_tables`, which documents this exact hazard and carries the tag for it. I checked the two alternatives first, and both are impossible rather than merely unattractive: the visibility setting is read from the scanning query's context, so the polluter cannot hide itself (verified: setting it to 0 on the scanner silences the log, setting anything on the creator cannot), and a blackholed address only turns an instant refusal into a connect timeout while still logging, which is why `04210` uses `192.0.2.1` and the tag. Test statements and the reference file are unchanged; the test runs in 0.23 s, so serializing it costs nothing.

signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/41240 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Seen under `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel)`: ``` Code: 159. DB::Exception: Timeout exceeded: elapsed 300200.551 ms, maximum: 300000 ms. (TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED) (query 20, line 69) ``` [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/114731/a5daee0848c43176efa72907a99ab173c49a6297/result_pr.json) **Root cause.** The bound that fires is the test's own `SET max_execution_time = 300`, and it sits at the top of the healthy distribution. Nothing else bounds the query: the server default is unlimited, and `tests/config` sets the setting only in `users.d/limits_fast.yaml`, linked for Fast test alone (`install.sh:293`). Measured on this check over the 90 days to 2026-08-14, n = 12736 passing runs: p50 23.4 s, p99 128 s, max 289.1 s, so 4% headroom. TSAN plus parallel-suite contention supplies the rest. Three CIDB timeouts share the signature, one on master. **Change.** I cut the fixture's row volume only (`LIMIT 65536` to `LIMIT 4096`); `4095` asserts the same `distinct x > 0` property `65535` did. Query-20 cost is row-linear over a fixed ~50 ms analysis floor (medians 655 ms at 65536 rows, 108 ms at 4096), and the cache under test is keyed on query text, so cutting rows removes execution noise only. All 100 `UNION ALL` branches, `max_threads = 32`, the 300 s bound and all four tags stay, and `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` is byte-identical. Sensitivity drops from ~13x the p50 to ~150x; the regression it names, its own "tens of minutes", is still caught. **Validation.** The failure is contention-driven and does not reproduce on an idle box, so I proved the mechanism deterministically: with the oracle tightened to 0.3 s, between the two medians, the unchanged file fails with the exact CI signature and the fixed file passes. 200 further runs pass across both files, randomization on and off. Side note, not fixed here: under this test's `enable_analyzer = 1` query 20 never reaches the sample-block cache, which only `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery` reads. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1441` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Transport join runtime filters across distributed plan stages
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114901 A join runtime filter is currently local to its fragment: the build side creates it and only `__applyFilter` sites in that fragment see it, so a fact table scan in another stage crosses its shuffle exchange in full even if the filter would have removed most rows. If `distributed_plan_join_runtime_filters` is enabled, each build task now ships its partial filter through a bounded fan-in cascade of merge stages, and the final stage broadcasts the complete merged union to the probe-side fragments, which apply it before the shuffle. Everything fails open: rows pass unfiltered until the merged filter arrives, so a filter that never arrives (or half-arrives) can't change results. Only inclusion filters travel, a shipped filter never costs more on the wire than one of the configured static size, and filters are only shipped when the estimated build key set is small compared to the receiving scan. This replaces an earlier prototype where the initiator collected and merged the filters and probe dispatch was rescheduled around filter readiness; here the partials just ride the exchange layer like any other stream, with no new worker operations, no dispatch changes, and no measurable planning cost. New settings: `distributed_plan_join_runtime_filters` (experimental, default off) is the only user-facing one; with it off, plans, wire traffic and results are identical to master, with one sizing-behavior exception: the exact phase of every runtime filter (including local ones under `enable_join_runtime_filters`) is now bounded by its actual key bytes rather than the hash-table buffer size, which moves the exact-to-bloom degradation point—earlier for long string keys (their bytes were previously uncounted) and later for short keys (the buffer, transiently up to ~2 MB per stream at the default 10000-row cap, no longer counts against the byte budget). Results are unchanged either way. The serialized plan additionally gains `join_runtime_filter_exact_bytes_limit`, which carries a transported filter's exact-phase byte budget to the workers. On public ClickHouse the transported exact-phase row cap is taken from the scan's row estimate, not from column-statistics NDV. HyperLogLog undershoots distinct keys, so using NDV as the cap overflowed complete key sets into bloom filters. An unindexed plan-time filter is also treated as unknown for transport sizing, so it keeps the settings geometry instead of letting statistics override it. ### TPC-H SF1000 r7g.4xlarge, ap-south-2, shared io2 volume read-only on every node, 2 warmups + 3 timed runs per variant, medians. Execution time only (planning excluded; it is identical with the setting on and off). | query | 4 nodes | 8 nodes | 16 nodes | exchange saved (4/8/16) | |---|---|---|---|---| | q17 | −77.6% | −65.6% | −60.8% | 202.7 / 202.6 / 202.6 GiB | | q02 | −71.9% | −67.1% | −45.9% | 51.7 / 51.6 / 41.5 GiB | | q20 | −63.7% | −49.6% | −33.9% | 34.6 / 33.7 / 25.3 GiB | | q11 | −42.9% | −27.0% | −17.7% | 25.1 / 24.8 / 23.6 GiB | | q07 | −23.3% | −18.6% | −16.6% | 37.2 / 37.2 / 36.9 GiB | The other ten campaign queries are ties, with one exception: q16 regresses (+0.15 s at 8 nodes, +0.39 s at 16) because a filter that ends up pruning nothing still gets broadcast and the broadcast grows with node count. The admission heuristic should catch this; tracked in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114901. ### TPC-H SF100 on a real network From an earlier prototype, included because it is the measurement over an actual NIC: 4× m8g.4xlarge, 9.53 Gbps between nodes, 0.116 ms RTT, medians of 5. The mechanism differs but the filters, admission logic, and apply sites are the same. | query | single node (s) | dist 4N off (s) | dist 4N on (s) | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | q02 | 0.448 | 1.214 | 0.446 | 2.72x | | q03 | 1.585 | 1.498 | 1.075 | 1.39x | | q07 | 1.582 | 1.501 | 1.186 | 1.27x | | q10 | 2.024 | 1.853 | 1.606 | 1.15x | | q11 | 0.317 | 0.593 | 0.293 | 2.02x | | q12 | 1.156 | 0.830 | 0.615 | 1.35x | | q17 | 1.321 | 3.206 | 0.831 | 3.86x | (q04, q09, q13, q14, q16, q19, q20, q22 were flat there; q05/q08/q15/q18 excluded for environment reasons unrelated to the transport.) Plan shapes for the two headline queries, from the SF100 evidence runs: *q17 without the transport, both `lineitem` scans run in full:* *q17 with it, both scans collapse ~996x before their shuffles:* *q02 without the transport, both 80M-row `partsupp` arms feed the join unpruned:* *q02 with it, the union reaches both `partsupp` scans and the cascade collapses:* ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Join runtime filters now travel across distributed plan stages when `distributed_plan_join_runtime_filters` is enabled: build-side tasks ship partial filters over the exchange layer and probe-side scans apply the merged union before their shuffle exchange, dramatically reducing the number of rows crossing the network. All failure modes are fail-open and results never depend on the filters.

signals.title: Extract reusable `ActionsDAG` lineage
signals.text: Extract a reusable `ActionsDAG` lineage computation into `actionsDAGUtils`. The new `traceActionsDAGLineage` traces every `ActionsDAG` output to at most one input via a single iterative, memoized traversal. Each hop is classified as `Identity`, `ValuePreserving`, or the weaker `DistinctValuesBound` (output NDV bounded by input NDV plus `ndv_delta`), and results are keyed by input/output positions, so they stay unambiguous under duplicated column names. `remapColumnStats` in the join-order optimizer is rewired onto the new API, replacing its hand-rolled `propagatesNdv`/`backTrackColumnsInDag` walk. Besides the extraction, this improves the call site: - One lineage walk per `ActionsDAG` instead of one full DFS per statistics column: complexity drops from `O(#stats × DAG)` to `O(DAG + #outputs)` when several columns carry statistics. - No wasted walks for statistics names that match no DAG input — previously the full DFS still ran and its result was discarded. - The common case of absent statistics stays free by construction: an explicit `mapped.empty()` guard skips the (now unconditional) lineage walk entirely. - The remap itself becomes a straight loop over the lineage vector with two hash lookups per traceable output, dropping the per-name set/map bookkeeping. The computed statistics values are unchanged: the hop classification is ignored by `remapColumnStats` (only traceability and `ndv_delta` matter there), and the `ndv_delta` logic — NULL-collapsing hops add one distinct value, with the same overflow guard — is identical. The position-based keying is a robustness property of the reusable API for future consumers; this consumer still keys statistics by column name. New unit tests cover the lineage kinds (`Identity` vs `ValuePreserving` vs `DistinctValuesBound`) and the position-based disambiguation of duplicated input/output names. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): - Not for changelog

signals.title: Hold the table lock across a lightweight UPDATE pipeline
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort (`Logical error: Part patch-... doesn't exist`) when a `DROP TABLE` runs concurrently with a lightweight `UPDATE` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table. The update now holds the table's shared lock until its patch part is committed, so the `DROP` waits instead of removing it. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #104431 as an unrelated `Upgrade check (amd_release)` failure with no fix on master: STID `3208-458f`, 4 hits on 4 unrelated PRs in 6 days ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=7970f08a82eaf2ad5217d57a7796ae1c5e920030&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade+check+%28amd_release%29)). **What breaks.** A lightweight `UPDATE` racing a `DROP TABLE` aborts the server, release builds included: `Transaction::commit`'s `modifyPartState` calls sit in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose catch-all is `std::terminate`. **Root cause.** `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute` takes `lockForShare` into a function-local holder and parks only the *storage* in the returned pipeline; `QueryPlanResourceHolder` keeps `storage_holders` and `table_locks` separately, so the lock dies when `execute()` returns, long before the sink commits the patch part. A concurrent `DROP` then takes the exclusive lock, `dropAllData()` clears `data_parts_indexes`, and the commit cannot find its own part. Reproducing it needs a UUID-less database (`Memory`/`Ordinary`), where `DROP` removes the data inline instead of deferring it, hence the intermittency. **The change.** Move the already-acquired lock into the pipeline's resources, as the INSERT path does at `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1297`. Three entry points: `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute`, `InterpreterAlterQuery::executeToTable` (lightweight rewrite), and `StorageAlias::updateLightweight`, which resolves a *different* storage and so needs the target's own lock, as `StorageAlias::read` does. `DELETE FROM` rewrites to `UPDATE` and is covered transitively. A concurrent `DROP` or `DETACH` now waits for an in-flight lightweight update, as it already does for `INSERT`. `TRUNCATE` is unaffected: for `MergeTree` it takes no exclusive lock (`InterpreterDropQuery.cpp:332`). **Validation.** New test `04905_lwu_drop_race_table_lock.sh`, one arm per fixed carrier. `sleep_before_commit_local_part_in_replicated_table_ms` opens the commit window, and each arm waits for the sink to log that pause before dropping, so an arm that never reaches the window reports that instead of passing quietly. Fails on master with the reported abort, passes with the fix, 50/50 runs green. <details> <summary>Both-directions matrix (every cell measured, Build IDs asserted against the running server)</summary> | binary | `UPDATE` | `ALTER ... UPDATE` | via `Alias` | |---|---|---|---| | master `1b90b99d` | ABORT | ABORT | ABORT | | interpreters-only `6ab7bac7` | pass | pass | ABORT | | full fix `33fc2917` | pass | pass | pass | The middle row is the control that shows the `StorageAlias` change is necessary: with both interpreter fixes applied, the alias arm is the only one that still aborts. The lock demonstrably serializes the two queries: `dropAllData: waiting for locks` moves from 1.47 s after the patch-part rename (inside the commit window) to 4.03 s after it (past the commit). Deadlock check: the change only extends the lifetime of a *Read* acquisition, and no sink on this path acquires the table lock at all. `update_sequential_consistency = 1`, which waits on the replication queue while the lock is held, and a following `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` both complete normally. </details>

signals.title: Do not mark granule empty when rows are removed from a chunk
signals.text: With `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1`, the read is split into PK-range layers (same machinery as FINAL); a boundary granule belongs to two layers, and the FilterSortedStreamByRange` border filter drops the other layer's rows. The query condition cache write in `FilterTransform` assumes a zero-rows-after-filter chunk contained every row of its mark ranges, so it recorded the whole granule as non-matching even though its rows in the other layer matched. Later queries with the same condition skipped the granule and returned too few rows. Cause of the `03821_join_use_nulls_outer_to_inner` flakiness. New flag `MarkRangesInfo::has_dropped_rows`, set (copy-on-write) by `FilterSortedStreamByRange` on chunks that lost rows; `FilterTransform` skips cache writes for flagged chunks. Suppresses only writes for boundary granules - reads and interior-granule writes keep working - and covers any future consumer of `readByLayers`. `04891_query_condition_cache_join_by_pk_ranges`: deterministic minimal repro (returned `1`, `0` before the fix; `1`, `1` after). All existing QCC and FINAL split-ranges tests pass, including `03821` with the triggering settings forced. <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix query condition cache poisoning by JOIN queries with query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, which made later queries with the same WHERE condition return too few rows.

signals.title: Preserve non-clonable sources for deferred set builds
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619#issuecomment-5230196558 The speculative ordered-set build used for index analysis consumed non-clonable source plans before it knew whether the set was complete. If a `ReadFromRemote` pipeline stopped on an unavailable shard before `Set::finishInsert`, the deferred build had no source left and `FunctionIn` received a not-ready set. Preserve non-clonable local sources by skipping the speculative index optimization and letting `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` perform the authoritative build. The regression test uses the deterministic five-part `test_unavailable_shard` reproducer from the linked issue comment and verifies that `ALL_CONNECTION_TRIES_FAILED` propagates normally. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix queries with an `IN` subquery over unavailable remote shards potentially raising the `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument` logical exception instead of the underlying connection exception.

signals.title: Add byte-weighted bytes_to_do and progress to system.mutations
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114678 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `system.mutations` now exposes byte-weighted mutation progress: `bytes_to_do` (the on-disk size of the data parts that still need to be mutated) and `progress` (an estimated finished fraction from 0 to 1, including the live fraction of the parts currently being rewritten). Part counts are a poor work proxy — parts are unequal in size and a regular merge can retire many pending parts at once — so the byte view is the honest one; the docs gain an "Estimating mutation progress" section with an equivalent parameterized-view recipe for older releases. Implements the conclusion of the research on the issue in two layers: **Columns** (`bytes_to_do` UInt64, `progress` Float64 in `system.mutations`): derived on read like `parts_to_do` — no persisted state, no replication protocol or znode format change. For plain `MergeTree` the sizes ride along the existing per-part scan in `getMutationsStatus`; for replicated tables the queue keeps returning name-only statuses under its state lock and the storage resolves sizes afterwards, so no parts lock is ever taken under the queue mutex (parts gone by then were retired and contribute nothing). The in-flight fraction comes from the merge list (`system.merges` rows with `is_mutation = 1`). Values are estimates by nature: a merge can retire pending parts at any moment, making `progress` jump forward. **Docs**: an "Estimating mutation progress" section on the `system.mutations` page explains why part-count percentages mislead and ships a parameterized-view recipe computing the same number on releases without the columns (the view was validated live against a running mutation, including a merge collapsing 9 pending parts mid-run), plus cross-links from `system.merges`, `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE`, and the knowledge base. The stateless test asserts exact values on both engines: with merges stopped (which parks mutation tasks), `bytes_to_do` equals the active parts' total size and `progress` is 0; after completion the entry reports 0 and 1. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Reuse the previous row's result for equal consecutive rows in Set execution
signals.text: The per-row execution of `x IN <set>` (`Set::executeImplCase`) hashes the full key for every row — SipHash128 for hashed multi-column keys. When the key columns are clustered (e.g. they are a primary-key prefix, so the data arrives sorted), consecutive rows form long runs of equal values, and the previous row's result can be reused after a cheap raw-byte comparison instead of repeating the hash+probe. With this change, when all key columns are non-nullable fixed-width (tuples are flattened element-wise), each row's raw bytes are compared with the previous row's, and on equality the previous result is reused, skipping the hash+probe entirely. Motivation: in SQL transpiled from PromQL selectors over `TimeSeries` tables, the per-row `id IN (tags subquery)` filter computes SipHash128 of a 24-byte `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` per row into a `HashSet<UInt128>`. On tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15s step, scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series, Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3), this filter took ~17.5% of CPU of a 30-day rate query scanning 69M rows. With this change the hashing disappears from the profile (~3% of cheap byte comparisons remain), and raw-selector benchmark queries improved 1.4–2.3x. The optimization is generic: any `IN` over clustered/sorted key columns benefits; for unclustered data the added cost is a few loads per row. Bitwise comparison is applied only to POD column layouts (fixed-width raw bytes in one contiguous buffer, tuples flattened element-wise), where bitwise equality implies key equality; strings, arrays, `Nullable` and other non-POD layouts keep the existing path. The new performance test `tests/performance/set_in_clustered_keys.xml` covers both the clustered case (runs of equal consecutive keys) and the unclustered regression control (consecutive rows always differ). Note: tsbench scale-64 validation is in progress; numbers will be added before merge. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up execution of `IN` over clustered (e.g. sorted by primary key) columns by reusing the previous row's result for equal consecutive rows.

signals.title: Fix ANY INNER JOIN with OR conditions depending on which table is built
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114354 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114676 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111645 `ANY INNER JOIN` returns one row per key, from both the left and the right table. With several `OR`-ed conditions in `ON`, the key of a condition was claimed through the used flag of the right row that the key is stored for — and one right row can be the stored row of a different key in each condition, so claiming it for one key silently retired the others. The result therefore depended on which side the hash table was built from. On the dataset from the issue, `t1 ANY JOIN t2` returned 3 rows and `t2 ANY JOIN t1` returned 6, and the same query returned 3 or 6 depending on `query_plan_join_swap_table`, which is a plan setting and must not change the result. `JoinUsedFlags` now keeps one flag array per condition, indexed by the cell of that condition's map, exactly as `per_offset_flags` does for a single condition, so the claim names the key of a condition rather than a right row. A left row visits every condition instead of stopping at the first match, so it may be joined once per condition whose key it claims — hence `ANY INNER JOIN` results are replicated now. The residual-condition path (`joinRightColumnsWithAdditionalFilter`) claims the same way, after applying the filter to the candidates of a key. The outcome is the union of the single-condition joins: a pair of rows matching through several conditions is joined once per condition, and the number of result rows no longer depends on the probe order, on the order the tables are written in, or on the plan. Deduplicating those pairs instead was measured to leave the row count dependent on which left row claims a key first, and so on the probe order — 39 runs out of 40 disagreed with the 40th at `max_threads = 8`. That semantics change moves two existing references, both for pairs that match through more than one condition: - `01660_join_or_inner`: `2 3 2 3` is returned twice, matching both `a2 = a3` and `b2 = b3`; - `03006_join_on_inequal_expression_fast_2`: `(1, 1, 1) INNER ANY JOIN (1, 1, 1) ON t1.a = t2.a AND (t1.b > 0 OR t2.b > 0)` returns its row twice, and in `ON t1.key = t2.key AND t1.a < t2.a OR t1.a = t2.a` one left row is now dropped because another left row with the same key claimed it, as single-condition `ANY INNER JOIN` already does. `SEMI`, `ANTI` and the `LEFT`/`RIGHT` forms of `ANY` are unaffected: their unit is the right row, which a per-row flag expresses exactly, and every branch added here is gated on `INNER` + `ANY`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ANY INNER JOIN` with several `OR`-ed conditions in the `ON` section returning a different number of rows depending on which table the hash table is built from, that is on the order the tables are written in and on the `query_plan_join_swap_table` setting. Such a join now returns one row per key of every condition, from both tables.

signals.title: Type `IN (subquery)` over `LowCardinality` consistently in the old analyzer
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114229 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100226 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from tuple. Expected Tuple(..., UInt8). Got Tuple(..., LowCardinality(UInt8))` when a `LowCardinality` column compared with `IN (subquery)` is read through `tuple(...)` across a subquery boundary and `enable_analyzer = 0`. With the old analyzer, `x IN (subquery)` over a `LowCardinality` column now returns `LowCardinality(UInt8)`, the same type as `x IN (literal list)` and the same as with `enable_analyzer = 1`. ### Description The old-analyzer half of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114229, whose test is tagged `no-old-analyzer`. Reproducer, broken since 26.6 and still broken on master: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (s LowCardinality(String)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY s; INSERT INTO t VALUES ('a'); SET enable_analyzer = 0; SELECT tuple(*) FROM (SELECT s, s IN (SELECT 'a') AS f FROM t); -- Code: 49. Unexpected return type from tuple. Expected Tuple(LowCardinality(String), UInt8). -- Got Tuple(LowCardinality(String), LowCardinality(UInt8)). (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` **Root cause.** The general typing rule wraps a result in `LowCardinality` only when at most one argument is a full `LowCardinality` column and no argument is a full ordinary column (`IFunctionOverloadResolver::getReturnType`, `src/Functions/IFunction.cpp:797`). The two passes over the same expression disagree: - during execution the set is a constant column (`ColumnSet` is always wrapped in `ColumnConst` since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100226) and a `Set`-typed argument counts as constant since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114229, so `in` returns `LowCardinality(UInt8)`; - during analysis the set from a subquery is not built yet, so `in` is replaced with `inIgnoreSet` and the left operand is passed twice as the stand-in for the missing set (`src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp`). Two full `LowCardinality` arguments fail the `num_full_low_cardinality_columns <= 1` condition, so the result types as plain `UInt8`. The outer query records `UInt8` for that column and the pipeline delivers `LowCardinality(UInt8)`, so `columnMatchesType` rejects the `tuple` result in `executeActionForPartialResult` during `ActionsDAG::updateHeader`. `DESCRIBE (subquery)` and `EXPLAIN header = 1` disagreeing on the type is the quick diagnostic. In a release build this is a query error; in debug and sanitizer builds it aborts the server. **Change.** The stand-in for the missing set is a constant `UInt8` instead of the left operand. It is indistinguishable from the real `Set` argument in every dimension the typing rule inspects — it is constant, so it is skipped by both `LowCardinality` counters; it is not `Nullable`, so it does not affect the null wrapper; and `FunctionIn::getReturnTypeImpl` only reads `arguments[0]`. Analysis and execution therefore agree by construction, for all eight `in` / `notIn` / `nullIn` / `notNullIn` × `global` variants and for every operand shape, not only the one in the reproducer. The `IgnoreSet` variants never look at their second argument. A `Set`-typed stand-in would mirror execution more literally, but `getRootActionsNoMakeSet` feeds window-definition expressions into an executed plan (`src/Interpreters/ExpressionAnalyzer.cpp:1562`), which can be serialized for distributed execution, and a `ColumnSet` with no set behind it would be dereferenced there. A `UInt8` constant cannot be. **Visible type change**, mirroring what https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114229 did for the analyzer: with `enable_analyzer = 0`, `toTypeName(x IN (subquery))`, `DESCRIBE` of such a subquery, `EXPLAIN` headers, and column types of `CREATE ... AS SELECT` over such an expression now show `LowCardinality(UInt8)` instead of `UInt8`. Values do not change. **Validation.** New stateless test `04894_in_subquery_lowcardinality_type_old_analyzer` asserts, for both analyzers, that the literal-set and subquery-set forms have the same type, that the type recorded for the subquery column is `LowCardinality(UInt8)`, and that `tuple(*)` over that column across a subquery boundary works, with `IN` / `NOT IN` `count()` controls. Its first two arms fail and the `tuple(*)` arm aborts a debug server without the change.

signals.title: Avoid repeated EXPLAIN ANALYZE clock lookups for staged processors
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Performance Improvement** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): - **Avoid repeated wall-clock registry lookups in **EXPLAIN ANALYZE** for multi-stage processors.** ### Why this matters - `StepWallClockRegistry::find()` is keyed by the query-plan step and processor group. - The cache pointer was stored, but the group stayed at its default value of `0`. - For non-default groups, such as aggregation finalization and join build/probe, the old code repeated the lookup for every task. - Normal query execution is unchanged because this registry is only used by **EXPLAIN ANALYZE**. ### Changes - **Store:** the group together with the clock pointer after lookup. - **Keep:** the existing retry behavior when no clock is found. - **Use:** the cached-clock alias consistently in the condition. ### Benchmark This is a focused microbenchmark of the cache lookup section, not end-to-end **EXPLAIN ANALYZE** latency. Setup: Apple arm64, Apple Clang `-O3`, stable group `1`, matching registry entry, 10,000,000 tasks, 9 rounds, median result. | Version | Registry lookups | Median time | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Before | 10,000,000 | 25.89 ms | 1.00x | | After | 1 | 3.21 ms | 8.07x faster | The lookup count is exact. Wall-clock time is machine-dependent. ### Validation - `git diff --check` - **Validation:** Focused cache lookup microbenchmark - **Validation:** Existing **EXPLAIN ANALYZE** coverage for aggregation and join stages

signals.title: SQLancer: track sqlancer main, deduplicate findings, fail the job on them
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes Not user-facing. ### Description Three fixes to the nightly SQLancer job (`NightlySQLancer`, every 3 days). #### 1. Fuzz `ClickHouse/sqlancer` `main`, not a hardcoded commit The image pinned `ClickHouse/sqlancer@a62ea509`, so oracle work landing in the fork never reached CI. Pointing the Dockerfile at a branch is not enough: praktika rebuilds an image only when its directory digest changes, so a branch fetched at image-build time freezes at whatever `main` was when the Dockerfile was last edited — worse than an explicit pin, because it silently lies about what is being fuzzed. Instead: - the image clones `main` as a **warm cache** and keeps `.git` plus the maven repository under `/sqlancer` (world-writable, so the job's non-root user can extend it); - `sqlancer_job.sh` **re-clones and rebuilds `main` at job start** (~1 min with the warm maven repo) and falls back to the baked build if GitHub or Maven is unavailable; - the resolved commit is printed and included in the job info, so a finding stays attributable after `main` moves. Overrides for a one-off run: `SQLANCER_REF`, `SQLANCER_REPO`, `SQLANCER_BUILD_AT_RUNTIME=0`. #### 2. Readable output: one artifact per finding, deduplicated Before, the job log was ~3600 progress lines for a 5h run plus, for every finding, the whole reproducer state dump that SQLancer's `AlsoWriteToConsoleFileWriter` mirrors to stderr — impossible to read, and the reproducers were only available as one tarball of everything. Now the console shows one progress line per ~5 minutes and a summary (~20 lines for a clean run); the full fuzzer output remains an artifact. Findings are reported individually **and** deduplicated: - Each `logs/clickhouse/databaseN.log` is exactly one finding (`StateLogger.logException` writes the stack trace plus that database's whole `CREATE`/`INSERT`/…/`SELECT` sequence, then the worker continues under a fresh database name), so each is copied out and attached as its own artifact. - New `ci/jobs/scripts/sqlancer_failures.py` fingerprints every finding as **(exception class + ClickHouse error code/name from the `Caused by:` chain, reporting oracle, first sqlancer stack frame)** and groups equal fingerprints. - The report gets one row per *distinct* failure with the individual findings and their logs nested underneath, plus `failures/analysis.txt` (all families, loudest first, and a per-finding index). The failure *message* is deliberately **not** part of the fingerprint: for most oracles it is the generated SQL, unique to every finding, which would defeat the dedup. To keep that safe, every family lists all of its occurrences by database name and up to three distinct *message shapes* (literals → `'S'`, numbers → `N`, generated identifiers such as `c0`/`t3`/`database7` → `id`), so a family that merged more than one bug is visible as such. The job info line becomes, for example: ``` sqlancer main @ 3a66cc5ce597; 1,407k queries; 43 finding(s) in 13 distinct failure(s): PivotedQuerySynthesisBase/Code 241 x20, NoREC/Code 241 x8, TLPDistinct/AssertionError x3, ... ``` and the rows: ``` Failure analysis [analysis.txt] PivotedQuerySynthesisBase / AssertionError / Code 241 (MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) / at SQLQueryAdapter.checkException:176 (x20) |- database0 [database0.log] \- ... TLPDistinct / AssertionError / at ComparatorHelper.assumeResultSetsAreEqual:127 (x3) |- database48 [database48.log] \- ... ``` If the analysis script itself fails, the job still fails and attaches the raw reproducer logs, so a bug in it can never swallow a finding. #### 3. A finding now marks the job failed Praktika derives the GitHub job conclusion from the job script's **exit code** (`res = run_code == 0` in `ci/praktika/runner.py`); the result file's status only drives the HTML report. Both SQLancer scripts exited 0 unconditionally, so a finding could not turn the nightly red. They now exit non-zero whenever anything was found: - a reproducer log; - a sanitizer report or `<Fatal>` message in the server logs (this job runs an ASan+UBSan build) — checked before the server is stopped, so a leak report emitted during shutdown does not turn every run red; - a dead or unreachable server; - a non-zero sqlancer exit code; - a run that produced no execution statistics at all (silently broken run). `sqlancer_pp_job.sh` additionally wrote the invalid status tokens `success`/`failure` instead of `OK`/`FAIL`, which made praktika render its result as "completed but unknown". Concretely, the [2026-08-13 nightly](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31674904130) reported **green** while the SQLancerPP job had failed on the `WHERE` and `NoREC` oracles. Its per-oracle logs are now attached to their own rows too. ### Testing The scripts' logic was exercised directly, without a real fuzzing run: - `ci/jobs/scripts/sqlancer_failures.py` against **43 real reproducer logs** from a saved SQLancer run: 43 findings → **13 distinct failures**, grouped the way they are actually triaged (PQS memory-limit noise x20, NoREC memory-limit x8, TLPDistinct row-count mismatch x3, TLPSetOp `UNION_DISTINCT` mismatch x1, TLPSetOp NPE x1, CODDTest Code 27 x1, …). Empty and missing log directories yield `no findings` and an empty fragment. - `ci/jobs/sqlancer_job.sh` end to end against stubbed `java`/`wget`/`git`/`mvn`/`clickhouse` binaries: clean run → `OK`, exit 0, 18 console lines; run with findings → `FAIL`, exit 1, 36 console lines and valid nested result JSON; UBSan `runtime error:` → `FAIL` while benign ASan boilerplate stays `OK`; server death, sqlancer crash, missing statistics, runtime-build failure (falls back with a warning), the 50-file upload cap, >10 MB log compression and a deliberately broken analysis script all behave as described. The real verification is the next nightly run of this workflow. ### CI validation (2026-08-14) Validated by dispatching `NightlySQLancer` twice from a throwaway branch on top of this one (short fuzz runs; branch deleted since). **[Run 31825081436](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31825081436) — clean path, 20 min fuzz.** Workflow conclusion `failure`, driven by SQLancerPP (see below). - Docker image with the new Dockerfile built (by this PR's own CI) and reused from the registry here. - Runtime clone + rebuild of `ClickHouse/sqlancer` `main`: **11 s**, commit `3a66cc5ce597`, no fallback (the warm maven repo in the image is doing its job). - **93 oracles** exercised, versus 31 with the old pinned commit. - 4 progress lines on the console for the whole fuzz run; job info `sqlancer main @ 3a66cc5ce597; 56k queries; no findings`; exit 0, job green. - The job's report entry is populated for the first time: status `OK`, `duration: 1243`, the info line and 5 artifact links. For comparison, the same entry in the [2026-08-13 nightly](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/REFs/master/45cb8371bbe63a39f7d0c655543563e8f15e5a40/result_nightlysqlancer.json) is `{"results": [], "links": [], "duration": null}`. - SQLancerPP went `failure` with per-oracle rows (`WHERE`, `QUERY_PARTITIONING` assertions; `FUZZING` → server not responding), each with its logs — and the **workflow status became `FAIL`**. The identical failure reported green on 2026-08-13. **[Run 31830811184](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31830811184) — failure path, 15 min fuzz** with `TextIndexDirectRead` re-included, since it reliably fires on the open ClickHouse#107186. - **37 findings deduplicated into 1 distinct failure**: `TextIndexDirectRead / java.lang.AssertionError / at ClickHouseTextIndexDirectReadOracle.check:95 (x37)`, one report row listing all 37 databases with 10 reproducer logs attached, plus the `Failure analysis` row with `analysis.txt`. - `analysis.txt` per-finding index carries the full assertion for each one (`ClickHouse#107186`, tokenizer, preprocessor, predicate, the diverging key sets and the DDL). - A downloaded reproducer (`database0.log`, 2035 lines) starts with the assertion plus stack trace and ends with the exact `CREATE TABLE ... INDEX idx (s) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha', preprocessor = lower(s))` + `INSERT` that reproduces it. - Job info `39k queries; 37 finding(s) in 1 distinct failure(s)`, job red, workflow `FAIL`. Two fixes came out of this validation and are included: the result-name bug above, and `SQLancerPP` no longer listing per-oracle logs that were never written (praktika replaces the whole job `info` with `WARNING: File [...] was not found`, which buried the result). One observation, not addressed here: the ASan+UBSan server writes ~10 MB of `DB::Exception` stack traces to stderr per 20 minutes (~150 MB projected over 5 h), from logging every failed fuzzer statement at error level. Dropping the mounted `log_level.xml` to `fatal` would remove it while keeping `<Fatal>` and sanitizer detection intact.

signals.title: Support Nullable(JSON) in tupleElement
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111234 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry: You can now access nested properties on a nullable JSON column, for example `col::Nullable(JSON).Id`. Previously this failed with `First argument for function tupleElement cannot be Nullable(JSON)`, which made it impossible to combine a cast to `Nullable(JSON)`, used to get `NULL` instead of an empty `{}` for a missing nested object, with property access on the result. Rows that are `NULL` in the outer column now yield `NULL` for the extracted path. ### Details `tupleElement` refused a `Nullable(JSON)` first argument in both `getReturnTypeImpl` and `executeImpl`. The refusal was specific to the JSON branch: | Probe | Before | | --- | --- | | `tupleElement(JSON, 'Id')` | works | | `tupleElement(Nullable(JSON), 'Id')` | `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` | | `Nullable(JSON)` as a type | legal; casts and NULL round-trip correctly | | `tupleElement(Nullable(Tuple(...)), 'a')` | already unwraps and propagates NULL | | `assumeNotNull(j).Id` | already produces the intended values | So the semantics were already implemented for `Tuple` and reachable via `assumeNotNull`; only the JSON branch rejected the input. This removes both throws and reuses the existing mechanism: - `getReturnTypeImpl` promotes the extracted path type with `makeExtractedSubcolumnsNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe` - `executeImpl` folds the outer null map into the extracted column with `NullableSubcolumnCreator` Both paths go through the same helper: `NullableSubcolumnCreator::create(DataTypePtr)` calls exactly that promotion function so the returned type and column cannot drift apart. Resulting behaviour: - a path with a type hint is promoted to `Nullable(T)` - an untyped path stays `Dynamic`, which cannot sit inside `Nullable` but can represent `NULL` itself, so the outer null map is applied to the `Dynamic` directly - `Nullable(QBit)` remains rejected, and the `Tuple` and `QBit` paths are untouched The two "must be Tuple, Nullable(Tuple), QBit, JSON or array of these" messages now also list `Nullable(JSON)`. ### Verification Added `04891_tuple_element_nullable_json`, covering const and materialized inputs, all-NULL input, mixed NULL/non-NULL rows, typed and untyped paths, a missing path, `Array(Nullable(JSON))`, chained access through a nullable sub-object, and the query from the issue. It also asserts `Nullable(QBit)` still throws, since that shares the type dispatch this changes. Verified against a `RelWithDebInfo` build of this branch: ``` SELECT tupleElement('{"Id":1}'::Nullable(JSON), 'Id') -> 1 SELECT CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(JSON)').Id -> NULL SELECT toTypeName('{"a":1}'::Nullable(JSON).a) -> Dynamic SELECT toTypeName(CAST('{"a":1}', 'Nullable(JSON(a UInt32))').a) -> Nullable(UInt32) SELECT (number % 2 ? NULL : '{"a":42}')::Nullable(JSON).a FROM numbers(4) -> 42, NULL, 42, NULL ``` Note the test orders by a companion `Int` column rather than by the result, because an untyped JSON path is `Dynamic` and `ORDER BY` on `Dynamic` is rejected by default (`allow_suspicious_types_in_order_by`).

signals.title: Fix `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` for single-column complex keys wrapped in `tuple`
signals.text: Since 25.12, the analyzer pass `InverseDictionaryLookupPass` (setting `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup`, enabled by default) rewrites `dictGet(dict, attr, key_expr) <op> const` into a comparison of the key expression against dictionary keys: either constants folded from `dictGetKeys` (`key_expr = const`, `key_expr IN [consts]`, or `0`), or the subquery form `key_expr IN (SELECT <key columns> FROM dictionary(dict) WHERE attr <op> const)`. The key expression is reused verbatim as the left-hand side, while all rewrite shapes produce bare key values on the right-hand side. A complex-key dictionary with a single key column accepts (and much existing SQL uses) the `tuple()`-wrapped call form `dictGet(..., tuple(k))` — for it, the rewrite pits a one-element `Tuple` against a scalar, and a query that works on every release before 25.12 fails with `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`. Multi-column keys are unaffected: `(k1, k2) IN (SELECT k1, k2 ...)` is the standard SQL form and the types line up. ## How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE dict_source (k UUID, k2 String, attr String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO dict_source VALUES ('11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111', 'a', 'foo'), ('22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222', 'b', 'bar'); CREATE DICTIONARY single_key_dict (k UUID, attr String DEFAULT '') PRIMARY KEY k SOURCE(CLICKHOUSE(TABLE 'dict_source')) LIFETIME(0) LAYOUT(COMPLEX_KEY_HASHED()); CREATE TABLE data (k UUID, k2 String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO data VALUES ('11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111', 'a'), ('33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333', 'c'); -- Must return 1, but fails since 25.12: SELECT count() FROM data WHERE dictGet('single_key_dict', 'attr', tuple(k)) = 'foo'; ``` On master the query fails in the constant-fold path: ``` Code: 43. DB::Exception: Illegal types of arguments (`Tuple(UUID)`, `UUID`) of function `equals`. (ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT) ``` On 26.3 (before the `dictGetKeys` constant fold existed) the same query fails in the subquery path with `Illegal type Tuple(UUID) of argument of function toUUID`. The workaround on affected releases is `SETTINGS optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup = 0`, which returns the correct result. The bare-key form `dictGet(..., k)` and multi-column keys work on all versions. ## The fix Normalize the key expression once, before both rewrite paths, when the dictionary key is composite with exactly one key column and the key expression resolves to a one-element tuple: - a syntactic `tuple(k)` call is replaced by its argument; - any other tuple-typed expression (e.g. a column of type `Tuple(UUID)`) is wrapped in `tupleElement(expr, 1)`. The rewrite still fires for these queries — the new test asserts the rewritten plans via `EXPLAIN SYNTAX run_query_tree_passes=1` for all three constant-fold shapes and both subquery shapes. Simple-key dictionaries are deliberately left alone: `dictGet(simple_dict, attr, tuple(id))` is rejected (`Illegal type Tuple(UInt64) of argument of function toUInt64`) even with the optimization disabled, so normalizing there would make otherwise-invalid queries succeed only while the optimization is on. A `Tuple`-typed dictionary key column cannot conflict with the unwrapping because dictionaries reject `Tuple` attribute types (`Unknown type Tuple(UUID) for dictionary attribute`). The new test `04891_optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup_single_key_tuple` covers the failing forms, the bare-key and two-column-key controls, a constant on either side of the comparison, and result equality with the optimization on and off. All existing `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` tests pass. ## Backport This is a regression in an official stable release (25.12) affecting all later releases, including 26.3 LTS. Please consider labeling for backport to 26.3 (`v26.3-must-backport`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` when `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` rewrites `dictGet` comparisons for complex-key dictionaries with a single key column and a `tuple()`-wrapped key expression.
